title: M1 — non-destructive history foundation
objective: Prove persistent edit layers and history end to end with a single-pixel tool, undo/redo, preview/restore, catalog reopen, desktop UI and a live external API.
context_summary: M1 is implemented and locally verified on the native M4 host plus automated exact-buffer, persistence, recovery, subprocess and bounded-work evidence. All IDs and dependencies are local to this file. The working foundation is documented in docs/engineering/m1-m2-results.md. M3 tool-module work remains a later milestone.

acceptance_criteria: Define stable asset/layer/snapshot/entry identities, ordered typed edit layers, immutable complete recipes, format markers, monotonic revisions and semantic action metadata.
Distinguish a layer from a history entry: adding or adjusting layer data produces one new snapshot/action while prior snapshots remain immutable. Keep original bytes external and read-only.
Define shared command validation, no-op/retry/conflict results and host transaction boundaries without UI types or a generalized module runtime.
Unit tests establish Original, two ordered layers, snapshot isolation, invalid payload rejection and complete state equality independently of the desktop.

steps: Test serialization/round-trip and immutable snapshot updates using small in-memory recipes.
Reject malformed IDs, missing payloads and unsupported internal formats without erasing data.
expected_results: Unit tests establish Original, two ordered layers, snapshot isolation, invalid payload rejection and complete state equality independently of the desktop.

acceptance_criteria: Implement replacement of one pixel with explicit integer input-stage coordinates and 8-bit sRGB channels, after source EXIF orientation is applied once.
Append a pixel layer for a real change; repeated replacements of the same location obey stack order and same-value changes report no-op.
Evaluate each snapshot from original pixels through ordered operations. Keep source fingerprints, color meaning, dimensions and snapshot identity attached to results.
Exact lossless-buffer fixtures prove that only the targeted pixel changes, the source remains unchanged, older snapshots still render and invalid coordinates/colors fail cleanly.

steps: Compare complete tiny asymmetric buffers and all EXIF orientations; avoid JPEG encode equality.
Test two edits at one pixel and edits at corners, invalid values, missing/changed sources and bounded image allocation.
expected_results: Exact lossless-buffer fixtures prove that only the targeted pixel changes, the source remains unchanged, older snapshots still render and invalid coordinates/colors fail cleanly.

acceptance_criteria: Select and pin SQLite access, create/open a local catalog and background-import a verified JPEG by reference with a stable asset ID and full fingerprint.

Store Original, immutable recipe snapshots, entries, current-entry/redo state, revision and request result in an atomic transaction. Pin a small internal format and detect incompatible catalogs explicitly.
Preserve source root/locator identity independently of edits; repeated filesystem aliases reuse the same asset while byte-identical different files are not silently merged.
Reopen and injected write/interruption failures preserve the last durable state, source bytes and stable IDs; no partial asset or falsely successful save is returned.

acceptance_criteria: Route pixel actions through the host service with expected revision and request ID; atomically persist the complete resulting stack and one attributed entry.
Undo follows undo parents; redo uses persisted navigation state. Both increment revision without appending Undo/Redo actions. New changes clear shortcut redo and retain every entry.
Restore copies a saved snapshot into a new Restore entry; undo returns to the preceding current state. Equivalent restores are explicit no-ops.
Expose paginated list/inspect/current/layer-state queries and immutable historical render inputs; stale revisions, wrong-asset entries and invalid retries cannot mutate state.
Service tests prove Original → A → B → undo/redo → restore A → C → reopen, retaining B and every intermediate snapshot with coherent navigation.

steps: Exercise every navigation transition, duplicate request, reused request ID with different payload and stale revision.
Inject commit failures and query a long history with bounded pages; verify attribution, sequence and immutable snapshot reconstruction.
expected_results: Service tests prove Original → A → B → undo/redo → restore A → C → reopen, retaining B and every intermediate snapshot with coherent navigation.

acceptance_criteria: Publish discoverable input/result schemas for catalog/import/state, pixel changes, history/navigation/preview, view state and job cancellation as available.
Implement bounded same-user local communication to one catalog owner, usable both by an external process while the GUI is open and by a headless session.
Keep authoritative mutations in the common service; use expected revisions, request deduplication, structured errors, explicit client-owned cancellation and sequence-aware reconnect.
Subprocess clients perform persistent edits, undo/redo and restore against one owner; retries/disconnects/competing owners produce no duplicate entries or lost updates.

expected_results: Subprocess clients perform persistent edits, undo/redo and restore against one owner; retries/disconnects/competing owners produce no duplicate entries or lost updates.
